newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 falls back led by broader issues.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 falls back led by broader issues.

text.p: The PX50 index fell on the Prague bourse on Wednesday while the major issue dominated RPIX edged slightly higher suggesting that most of the downard pressure came from less heavily capitalised shares.
Trading remained thin but overall turnover at 757 million crowns was the highest this week.

The largest Czech savings bank, Ceska Sporitelna, was unchanged on Wednesday at 350 crowns per share with bids seen on the over-the-counter market on small blocks at 345 and on larger blocks (over 30,000 pieces) at 360.
On Tuesday Sporitelna announced plans to shed at least 5,000 jobs over the next five years, cutting its work force by a quarter.
Dealers said the announcement was unlikely to affect the share price immediately but believed it would exert a positive effect in the long term.

"I don't see this affecting the price right now but maybe later on. It could be positive in a fundamental sense, reducing costs and the income per emplyee ratio," said Ivan Kusacek, a dealer at Zivnostenska Banka in Prague.
